subject: Post-call: onramp technical checklist & private connectivity items
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Brown <sam.brown@dataflux.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: onramp technical checklist & private connectivity items

Hi Sam — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap of what we covered and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Summary of ask
- DataFlux wants private connectivity for inference (VPC endpoint preferred), strict egress controls, and mTLS to our private deployment.
- You're evaluating embeddings + a lightweight reranker for search relevancy, plus structured output for downstream actions.

Agreed next steps (owners & target dates)
1) Kicked off basic checklist and attachments (this thread) — Tessa — today
2) Provide VPC endpoint requirements + IP ranges for allowlist — Karthik — by 26 Aug
3) Share recommended auth pattern (short-lived tokens / service account flow) and SDK quickstart — Monica/Karthik — by 26 Aug
4) Provide sample mTLS cert format and rotation guidance — Karthik — by 26 Aug
5) Follow-up call to confirm rollout plan (30 min) — schedule after 26 Aug (Sam/Tessa)

Notes from the call (technical highlights)
- Networking: You prefer a customer-managed VPC endpoint (AWS PrivateLink) and want traffic to exit via your NATs (egress control).
- DNS: split-horizon DNS will be needed (private DNS zone pointing to endpoint).
- mTLS: DataFlux would like mutual TLS using their internal CA if possible.
- SDK/auth: We recommend a service account + short-lived bearer tokens (token exchange) for server-side calls.
- Embeddings & rerank: We suggested embeddings stored in your vector DB; reranker can run on Redwood Dedicated for low-latency scoring.
- Structured output/tool calling: Use function-calling schema; we can provide prompt templates and JSON schema validation hooks.

Attachments referenced: redwood-private-connectivity-design.pdf (high-level), sample onboarding checklist (inline).

Next immediate ask for you: can you confirm the internal CA certificate chain and an initial list of 3 egress IPs or the VPC CIDR block so we can draft the endpoint config?

Thanks — will loop Karthik in for specifics.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
T: +1 (415) 555-0134
--
Redwood Inference — Production-grade LLM inference for teams

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Hi Sam / team — passing along the concrete checklist and implementation notes from the platform/infra side. I kept vendor-agnostic steps where possible.

1) VPC endpoint (PrivateLink or equivalent)- Requirements:
   - Provide the VPC CIDR or the 3 NAT egress IPv4 addresses you mentioned.
   - We will provide an endpoint service name and an internal IP for your routing table.
   - DNS: configure a private hosted zone (split-horizon) mapping the Redwood endpoint CNAME to the private IP we provide. If you're on AWS PrivateLink we recommend enabling private DNS so SDK calls resolve internally.
   - Ports: outbound HTTPS (443) only; our infra will accept TLS connections on 443, no custom ports required.

2) IP allowlist / egress- Guidance:
   - If you use NAT egress IPs, allowlist those three addresses on your side.
   - Alternatively, you can pin by VPC endpoint ENI CIDRs once we provide them.

3) Mutual TLS (mTLS)- Certs & rotation:
   - We support customer-supplied CA chains for client cert validation. Please provide PEM-encoded CA bundle (root + intermediates).
   - Client certs should be X.509 (PEM). We validate the client cert on connect and map the subject to a service account.
   - Rotation: recommend short-lived client certs (90 days) and an automated rollout using your existing cert management platform (ACME/HashiVault/Cloud CA). We can support an automated pull model (you upload new certs to a shared S3/secure endpoint) or a push via our onboarding API.

4) Auth & SDK pattern- Recommendation:
   - Create a Redwood service account for DataFlux that’s bound to your org's project.
   - Use a token-exchange flow: your infra exchanges a signed assertion (OIDC JWT) for a short-lived Redwood bearer token (TTL ~15m–1h). This avoids long-lived API keys and maps cleanly to RBAC and audit logs.
   - SDK quickstart: server-side SDK uses the bearer token in Authorization: Bearer <token>. Client-side web/mobile usage should go through your backend to avoid exposing tokens.

5) Structured output & tool-calling- Integration notes:
   - Provide a JSON schema for the top-level `action` object you mentioned. We will bind function-calling (structured output) to that schema and run JSON schema validation in the runtime.
   - For any side-effects (webhook/callouts) we recommend a signed callback pattern (HMAC + timestamp) and validating on your end.

6) Embeddings & reranker pattern- Suggestions:
   - Embeddings: precompute and store in your vector DB (we can provide a batch embedding job via our SDK). Use an embeddings model with known cost/latency profile (we will recommend a specific model in a follow-up if you share expected query volume).
   - Reranker: run reranker on Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool) to keep latency consistent for scoring top-K results. If you need very high throughput we can advise on dedicated autoscaling knobs.

7) Ops & observability- What we'll provide:
   - Token-level traces for request latency, per-route cost breakdowns, and embedding call metrics.
   - Audit logs for authentication events (token exchange, cert validations).

Attachments included in this mail: vpc-endpoint-terraform.tf (example), mtls-cert-sample.txt (pem skeleton). I can also drop a minimal terraform module if you want to try a PoC quickly.

Implementation timeline (estimate)
- With cert chain + NAT IPs: PoC routing + DNS validation in ~3 business days.
- Full PoC (token exchange + basic rerank flow): 1–2 weeks depending on your engineering availability.

Open questions for you
- Confirm preferred cert delivery method (S3 upload vs secure upload endpoint).
- Confirm if you want us to enable private DNS automatically for PrivateLink.

Happy to hop on a 30-min technical call to walk through the terraform example and cert exchange flow. Suggest Thu 26 Aug or Fri 27 Aug morning PST.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
